title: Director of Maintenance
description:
Director of Maintenance Job Summary: The primary purpose of this position is to maintain the orderly functioning of all equipment in the facility including the kitchen, laundry, heating, air conditioning, and elevators as well as purchasing necessary supplies for repairs, maintenance, and emergencies within budgetary guidelines.

QUALIFICATIONS:

A high school diploma is preferred.

Basic knowledge of plumbing, electricity, and heating and air-conditioning. Licensure or certification in any of these areas is preferred.

JOB REQUIREMENTS

Must be physically and mentally capable of performing routine job duties.

Must have good problem solving and trouble-shooting abilities.

Be personable with residents, families, and staff in a professional and cooperative manner.

Must have compassion, tolerance, and understanding for the elderly.

Knowledge of JCAHO, NFPA , OSHA, regulations relevant to building design, maintenance, and proper functioning of all equipment.

Must be able to lift, push, pull, move equipment, supplies, linens, etc in excess of fifty (50) pounds as required.

MAIN DUTIES:

Support the facility's philosophy of care and strive to achieve its goals and objectives.

Be on call seven (7) days a week, 24 hours a day to troubleshoot in any and all kinds of emergencies or urgent repairs.

Maintain and document schedule of hot water checks in residents' rooms, baths, showers, and all general hot water sources in the facility.

Assure the proper maintenance and running condition of all electricity and plumbing in the entire facility including (but not limited to):

a) the kitchen area

b) the laundry room

c) the residents' rooms

d) the nurses' stations

e) all common areas including bathrooms, showers, etc.

Assure the proper maintenance and running condition of all equipment in the building including (but not limited to):

a) all kitchen appliances and machinery

b) all laundry appliances and machinery

c) all nurses' call station systems

d) air handlers

e) forced air units

f) boilers and heating units in the boiler room

g) sump pumps

h) emergency generator--check bi-weekly at load and monitor automatic weekly self-check

i) fire alarm system

j) elevators

Check and replace air filters in all units in the building and on the roof.

Connect any equipment up request.

Schedule with contracted companies and observe periodic inspections on:

a) fire alarm system (annually)

b) sprinkler system (quarterly)

c) fire extinguishers (annually)

d) ANSUL system (bi-annually)

e) generator (bi-annually)

Perform all repairs that do not fall under the purview of housekeeping.

Check periodically and document the temperature in residents' rooms.

Maintain up-to-date knowledge of any changes in JCAHO, Federal, and State regulations, modify department policies to assure compliance, and in-service all effected personnel accordingly.

Prepare a plan of correction as required by State and Federal surveys and submit them to the Administrator for approval.

Implement any plan of correction as required by State and Federal surveys in the building maintenance department.

Furnish information regarding residents only to authorized agencies or people.

Maintain all housekeeping and laundry equipment in operating condition.

Supervise all construction, renovation, and remodeling in the building.

Supervise repairs and routine maintenance of the building and all the departmental equipment.

Follow established fire, disaster, safety, infection control, and evacuation policies and procedures.

Perform other related duties as directed by the Administrator.

title: IP, Infection Preventionist
description:
Position Summary: 

Develops and implements an ongoing infection prevention and control program to prevent, recognize, and control the 
onset and spread of infections in order to provide a safe, sanitary, and comfortable environment.
Establishes facility-wide systems for the prevention, identification, reporting, investigation, and control of infections 
and communicable diseases of residents, staff, and visitors. 
Develops and implements written policies and procedures in accordance with current standards of practice and 
recognized guidelines for infection prevention and control.
Oversees the facility’s antibiotic stewardship program. 
Oversees resident care activities that increase risk of infection (i.e., use and care of urinary catheters, wound care, 
incontinence care, skin care, point-of-care blood testing, and medication injections). 
Leads the facility’s Infection and Prevention Control Committee. Develops action plans to address opportunities for 
improvement.
Participates on the facility’s QAA Committee. Performs duties as assigned.
Implements an annual infection control risk assessment process and participates in the facility’s annual facility 
assessment review process.

Reviews and/or revises the facility’s infection prevention and control program, its standards, policies, and procedures 
annually and as needed for changes to the facility assessment to ensure they are effective and in accordance with 
current standards of practice for preventing and controlling infections.
Provides education related to infection prevention and control principles, policies, and procedures to staff, residents, 
and families (where appropriate).
Ensures public health is notified of reportable diseases.
Collaborates with other departments in fulfilling requirements related to occupational health and safety. (I.e. 
employee health).
Maintains documentation of infection prevention and control program activities.
